Verdict: ACCEPT for the closed-component receiver theoremThe receiving tiles are distinct even when full, and the constructed set  $X$  satisfies
$$|X|=2C_{01}-J_c.$$
Under the stated nonexceptional AA hypotheses, with every count restricted to the chosen closed components inside one fixed full endpoint component, this gives
$$|X|=2(M_{01}-M_{10})\ge 8\ell.$$
I checked the direction-tag argument and the whole-source closed-owner exclusion needed from the intervening note; I have not assumed its pending review accepted them.There is one scope correction to make in the receiver note’s §4: replace “For arbitrary port graphs” before equation (4) byFor any chosen union of closed components of the specified port graph, without imposing AA.The identity is correct with the note’s standing closed-component restriction. It is false in general if the counts include open components. This correction preserves the receiver theorem and its AA consequence.My acceptance concerns the written theorem under the complete-source geometry and profile catalogue stated in the supplied notes. It does not certify execution of the Lean file or fixtures.1. Precise objects and the dependency being usedThroughout this audit, ownership means original source ownership.Let  $\mathscr S$  be the chosen collection of closed specified port components, and let  $E_{01}(\mathscr S)$  be its neutral phase01-to-phase01 contacts. Write
$$C_{01}=|E_{01}(\mathscr S)|.$$
For a contact  $e$ , use its unique active-to-passive orientation and write
$$q=p+d,\qquad
A_e=\{p+s,p+2s\},\qquad
z_e=p+s+d,\qquad
w_e=p+2s+d.$$
The original phase01 geometry gives the physical tile
$$Q_e=A_e\sqcup\{z_e,w_e\},$$
with  $A_e$  the active owner’s exact original endpoint profile in  $Q_e$ .For the stronger exclusion, define
$$P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}
=
\bigcup_{\substack{F\text{ an original phase01 owner}\\
F\text{ on any closed specified port component}}}
P_F^{\mathrm{orig}}.$$
This includes the entire original endpoint set of each such owner, and includes owners on unchosen closed components.The required dependency is
$$z_e\in P\setminus P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}.
\tag{D}$$
Merely excluding closed owners’ terminal endpoints would be insufficient for the new receiver-injection proof: that proof needs to exclude ownership of  $z_e$  by another active owner’s regular predecessor pair.Support retention forces  $z_e$  to be an original endpointAs stated in the supplied support note §1,  $z_e$  is a mandatory original support of both incident sources, with distinct persistent endpoint anchors
$$z_e-d=p+s,\qquad z_e-s=q.$$
If it were not consumed into  $P$ , mandatory retention would leave a selected support with two persistent endpoint neighbours, violating the stipulated degree condition. Thus  $z_e\in P$ .Because  $z_e$  is an original support of each incident source, its original owner is neither incident source. This conclusion introduces no new owner-freshness assumption: it distinguishes the owner only from those two particular incident sources.2. The direction-tag proof and whole-owner exclusion are sound2.1 The eight-frame argument allows recurring ownersBoth terminals of one original phase01 U have the same directed stem-to-bar direction. Thus assigning that direction to every endpoint of the owner gives a consistent tag. Unequal stem heights do not change the direction.Normalize the common forced point to  $0$ , and normalize the first contact to
$$s=N=(-1,0),\qquad d=E=(0,1).$$
Use one transformation for both contacts, transporting the original physical partition with it.The first active owner supplies
$$(1,-1),\quad(0,-1),\quad(-1,-1),$$
all tagged  $N$ . For a second frame  $(s',d')$ , its active stencil is
$$-s'-d',\quad -d',\quad s'-d',$$
tagged  $s'$ , and its passive stencil contains
$$-s',\quad -s'+d',$$
tagged  $d'$ .I checked every nonidentical frame in the supplied table:Second frameConflicting second-owner stencilShared endpointConflicting tag $(S,E)$ Active $(0,-1)$  $S$  $(S,W)$ Passive $(-1,-1)$  $W$  $(E,S)$ Active $(-1,-1)$  $E$  $(E,N)$ Active $(1,-1)$  $E$  $(N,W)$ Passive $(1,-1)$  $W$  $(W,S)$ Active $(-1,-1)$  $W$  $(W,N)$ Active $(1,-1)$  $W$ Each shared endpoint already has tag  $N$ . If the two displayed occurrences had the same original owner, their tags would agree. If they had different original owners, endpoint disjointness would prohibit the shared endpoint. Thus neither interpretation permits the conflict.This is exactly why owner recurrence does not defeat the argument. The proof never assumes different contacts have different owners.The only remaining frame is  $(N,E)$ . Equal forced points and equal frames determine
$$p=z-s-d,\qquad q=z-s.$$
Original ownership is unique, and the actual neutral receiver has a unique partner for each terminal. Hence the contact itself is identical.The eight-frame exhaustion is therefore a valid universal local argument. Its dimensional input is the minimum terminal stencil, including  $p+2s$ , rather than a search over bounded source dimensions.2.2 The exclusion covers every original endpoint role of a closed phase01 ownerLet  $F$  be the original owner of  $z_e$ , and suppose  $F$  is phase01. The two perpendicular neighbours
$$z_e-d,\qquad z_e-s$$
belong to the incident sources, so they are foreign to  $F$ .The stated phase01 catalogue exhausts the possibilities as follows.Nonterminal stem endpoint. Such a point has two opposite original neighbours belonging to  $F$ . Every opposite cardinal pair meets the two perpendicular directions  $\{-d,-s\}$ . Therefore one required own neighbour would be one of the two foreign endpoints above, contradicting original endpoint disjointness.Bar endpoint. Its phase01 bar receiver has an original  $4P0T$  profile. Since the physical partition is fixed, the original tile containing  $z_e$  is precisely  $Q_e$ . A full original profile there would overlap the active owner’s pair  $A_e$ . This also handles outer bar corners, where an argument using only the number of own neighbours would need care.Terminal endpoint. This is the only remaining possibility. But  $Q_e$  already contains the three distinct endpoints
$$A_e\cup\{z_e\}.$$
If  $F$  belongs to any closed specified port component, both its terminals have actual neutral receivers with exactly two endpoints. The fixed tile containing this terminal cannot simultaneously have at least three endpoints.Consequently  $F$  cannot be any closed phase01 owner, proving (D).This proof is independent of which closed components were chosen. It excludes a closed owner on another chosen curve, an unchosen curve, or the same curve. It also establishes the required whole-source exclusion, rather than only a terminal exclusion.These arguments validate the necessary portion of the intervening dependency without using its later paragraph that cites the receiver theorem itself.3. Receiver injection is valid, including both ports of one active ownerSuppose
$$Q_e=Q_f.$$
Different active original ownersTheir exact original pairs  $A_e,A_f$  are disjoint by endpoint disjointness. Both have cardinality two and lie in the same four-point tile, so
$$Q_e=A_e\sqcup A_f.$$
Since  $z_e\notin A_e$ , it follows that
$$z_e\in A_f.$$
But the active owner of  $f$  is a phase01 owner on a chosen closed component. This contradicts (D).The argument works for a full receiver. Indeed, the hypothetical coincidence itself forces the tile to be full; the contradiction comes from closed-owner exclusion.The same active original ownerThere are exactly two cases.If the contacts use the same terminal, the terminal’s actual neutral receiver has a unique other endpoint and hence a unique partner. The contacts are identical.If they use the two different terminals, their predecessor pairs lie on the two distinct original stems. Under the stipulated width-at-least-six geometry, the stems’ transverse separation exceeds the one-step span of a physical  $2\times2$  tile. Thus those pairs cannot occupy the same physical tile.Independent terminal heights affect longitudinal positions, not this transverse separation.Therefore
$$e\longmapsto Q_e$$
is injective on the chosen closed-contact collection.This proof handles a double-active owner explicitly. It does not infer contact uniqueness from owner uniqueness, and it imposes no freshness requirement on any other original owner.4. The second endpoint of a full receiver also avoids all closed phase01 ownersSuppose  $Q_e$  is full, and let  $F$  be the original owner of  $w_e$ .First,  $F$  cannot be the active owner: that owner’s exact original profile in  $Q_e$  is  $A_e$ . Exactness is essential here.Suppose instead that  $F$  is another closed phase01 owner. Its original profile in  $Q_e$  must avoid  $A_e$ . The stated catalogue leaves only these possibilities:Original phase01 profile of  $F$  in  $Q_e$ ContradictionFour endpointsIt overlaps  $A_e$ .Two endpointsIt must be the complementary pair  $\{z_e,w_e\}$ , so  $F$  owns  $z_e$ , contradicting (D).One endpointIt is a terminal of  $F$ , whose actual receiver must have exactly two endpoints;  $Q_e$  has four.For the pair case, cardinality alone already forces the complement: two endpoints avoiding a fixed two-element subset of a four-element tile must be the other two points. The adjacent-pair catalogue is consistent with this conclusion, but no further pair orientation is needed at this step.This explicitly resolves both requested full profiles: $2+2$ : the opposite pair’s owner cannot be closed phase01, because it owns  $z_e$ . $2+1+1$ : either opposite endpoint attributed to a closed phase01 singleton would be that owner’s terminal, contradicting the actual full receiver.If one owner owns both opposite points, its exact profile is a pair; they cannot be treated as two independent singleton profiles of that same owner.Thus
$$w_e\notin P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}$$
whenever  $Q_e$  is full. The argument includes the passive incident owner and arbitrary unchosen closed phase01 owners.5. The exact cardinality and the same-component assertion followDefine
$$X_e=(P\cap Q_e)\setminus A_e,\qquad
X=\bigcup_{e\in E_{01}(\mathscr S)}X_e.$$
Every  $Q_e$  contains  $A_e\cup\{z_e\}$ . Hence
$$|X_e|=
\begin{cases}
1,&Q_e\text{ nonfull},\\
2,&Q_e\text{ full}.
\end{cases}$$
Receiver injection gives distinct tiles. Because these are cells of one fixed physical partition, they are disjoint. Accordingly the union defining  $X$  is disjoint, and
$$\begin{aligned}
|X|
&=J_c+2(C_{01}-J_c)\\
&=2C_{01}-J_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}$$
The subtraction-free form is
$$|X|+J_c=2C_{01}.$$
The preceding exclusions give
$$X\cap P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}=\varnothing.
\tag{2}$$
The transport of the partition is doing real work. In the normalized frame, for example,
$$Q_e=\{(0,-1),(-1,-1),(0,0),(-1,0)\}.$$
One must preserve this transported tile instead of resetting parity at the new origin. The supplied notes expressly preserve it. Consequently the later disjointness argument compares actual cells of the original partition.Localization to the same full endpoint componentThe relevant endpoint adjacencies are
$$z_e\sim p+s,\qquad
w_e\sim p+2s\quad\text{when }Q_e\text{ is full},$$
together with
$$p+2s\sim p+s\sim p\sim q.$$
All points in these chains are persistent endpoints whenever they are used.Thus every point of  $X_e$  lies in the full endpoint component containing the original contact. If the chosen curves lie in a fixed component  $c$ , then
$$X\subseteq P(c)\setminus P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}.
\tag{3}$$
The exact equality in (1) is the cardinality of the constructed set  $X$ . For the entire outside-endpoint set, the warranted conclusion is
$$\left|P(c)\setminus P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}\right|
\ge 2C_{01}-J_c.$$
There may be additional outside endpoints elsewhere in  $c$ .6. The common  $H$  pool and the AA deduction are valid6.1 Nonfull receivers give distinct local  $H$  contributionsIf  $Q_e$  is nonfull, its three endpoints are exactly
$$p+s,\quad p+2s,\quad z_e.$$
Its missing corner  $w_e$  neighbours both  $p+2s$  and  $z_e$ , so it cannot be selected. Thus  $Q_e$  is an actual  $3P0T$  tile and contributes an  $L_3$  unit to  $H$ , as used in the support note §4.The nonfull receivers are distinct. Moreover, the component argument above puts their endpoint triples in the same component  $c$ . Therefore the stop map itself localizes:
$$J_c\le H(c).
\tag{4}$$
This local statement remains valid even if unrelated components have nonzero defects.For the joint budget, the support note’s separation argument is also sound. A  $D$ -stop, a  $C_0$ -stop, and a  $J_{01}$ -stop carry exact original pairs from the stipulated different original source classes. If two such nonfull stopping tiles coincided, their disjoint original pairs would fill the tile, contradicting nonfullness. Together with the established within-class counts, this gives
$$D+C_0+J_{01}\le H.$$
Using
$$B=D+C_0+C_1+E_1,\qquad C_1,E_1\le A,$$
and  $J_c\le J_{01}$ , one obtains
$$B+J_c\le 2A+H.
\tag{5}$$
Combining (5) with  $|X|+J_c=2C_{01}$  yields exactly
$$2C_{01}+B
=|X|+J_c+B
\le |X|+2A+H.$$
This spends the common  $H$  capacity once. A full receiver contributes endpoints to  $X$ , but creates no  $H$  unit.A useful proof-detail clarification is that
$$H(c)=0\Longrightarrow J_c=0$$
follows from the stronger local stop bound (4). The displayed inequality  $B+J_c\le2A+H$ , by itself, would not establish this unless one also controlled  $A$ . No assumption  $A=0$  is needed here.6.2 Incidence counting on the chosen closed componentsLet  $C_{\mathrm{mix}}$  count mixed-phase neutral edges in the chosen closed union. Every original-owner vertex there has degree two, so
$$2M_{01}=2C_{01}+C_{\mathrm{mix}},
\qquad
2M_{10}=2C_{10}+C_{\mathrm{mix}}.$$
Subtracting gives
$$C_{01}-C_{10}=M_{01}-M_{10}.
\tag{6}$$
These equations count original owners once and their two port incidences separately. Legitimate parallel edges are counted individually. Thus neither owner recurrence through its two ports nor two-vertex cycles cause a counting defect.For clarity, the correction needed to the phrase “arbitrary port graphs” is substantive if that phrase is intended to include open-component counts. In a general degree-at-most-two port graph, let  $U_{01},U_{10}$  count unused port incidences. Then the correct formula is
$$2(C_{01}-C_{10})
=
2(M_{01}-M_{10})-(U_{01}-U_{10}).$$
An isolated phase01 vertex already shows why the uncorrected general assertion fails: its edge difference is zero and its owner difference is one. On the chosen closed union, both unused-port counts vanish, giving (6).6.3 Same-component AA conclusionNow restrict everything to the chosen closed components inside one fixed full endpoint component  $c$  satisfying the stipulated nonexceptional AA hypotheses.The established AA property makes every phase10 owner in a closed port component double-active. Since a neutral edge has exactly one active endpoint, no neutral edge can join two such phase10 owners:
$$C_{10}=0.$$
Consequently (6) gives
$$C_{01}=M_{01}-M_{10}.$$
The accepted turning inequality applies componentwise and hence to this chosen collection:
$$M_{01}-M_{10}\ge4\ell.$$
Also  $H(c)=0$ , so the local stop bound gives  $J_c=0$ . Substituting into the exact count,
$$\boxed{
|X|
=2C_{01}
=2(M_{01}-M_{10})
\ge8\ell,
\qquad
X\subseteq P(c)\setminus P_{\mathrm{cl},01}^{\mathrm{all}}.
}$$
Choosing a single closed component gives its individual eight-endpoint consequence. Choosing several gives a simultaneous count because receiver injection holds across the whole collection. Unchosen closed phase01 owners remain excluded throughout.Formal and evidentiary scopeThe eleven supplied Lean statements are compatible with this proof structure, but they are scoped local, logical, and arithmetic statements. In particular:receiver_map_injective_of_owner_separation assumes the two geometric owner-separation implications;outside_endpoint_count assumes the contact partition and endpoint count;phase_edge_incidence assumes the degree-two incidence equations;AA_stops_vanish assumes the stop-to-boundary bound.The physical arguments above supply the corresponding written obligations. I make no compilation or axiom-audit certification.The reported fixtures provide no coverage of closed phase01-to-phase01 contacts. The partial four-phase01 polygon also supplies no complete feasible realization. The acceptance rests on the written universal arguments: the exhaustive direction cases, original profile exclusion, exact four-point packing, stem separation, fixed partition, and local budget map.The result counts distinct endpoint positions and distinct receiving tiles. Recurring outside owners remain permitted, and no additional reserve payment follows from this count alone. Full finite coefficient one and rectangular-grid triple equality remain open.
